quizName: DMV Practice Test #13 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white backgrounds and black letters. They tell you the traffic rules for that road. You must follow these signs.

questions.question: When stopping behind a vehicle, you should:

options.text: Stop far behind the vehicle, then slowly creep up.
Stay well behind the vehicle.
Make a quick stop right behind the vehicle.
Stay about four car lengths behind the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay well behind the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Stay a safe distance behind the vehicle in front of you. The vehicle may back up suddenly. You also need room to move if another vehicle comes toward you from behind.

questions.question: When turning left, you should:

options.text: Press the right handgrip.
Press the left handgrip.
Press both handgrips at the same time.
Not press either handgrip.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the left handgrip.
questions.explanation: To turn left, press the left handgrip. This makes the motorcycle lean the right way for the turn.

questions.question: You will ______ hear a tire going flat.

options.text: Always
Usually
Frequently
Seldom

questions.correctAnswerText: Seldom
questions.explanation: You will rarely hear a tire going flat on a motorcycle. Instead, you will notice the way the motorcycle handles change.

questions.question: When riding, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your arms straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn just your head and eyes to look through turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head and eyes to look through turns.
questions.explanation: Look where you want to go through a turn. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They warn you about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: More than half of all crashes:

options.text: Occur at speeds greater than 35 mph.
Happen at night.
Are caused by worn tires.
Involve riders who have operated the involved motorcycle for less than six months.

questions.correctAnswerText: Involve riders who have operated the involved motorcycle for less than six months.
questions.explanation: More than half of motorcycle crashes involve riders with less than six months of experience on that motorcycle.

questions.question: Fatigue can be increased by:

options.text: Stopping frequently.
Riding in cool weather.
Being comfortable during your ride.
Starting a ride late in the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding in cool weather.
questions.explanation: Cool, windy, or rainy weather can make you tired while riding. To stay alert, dress for the weather and limit your riding to about six hours per day. Stop and rest at least every two hours. Avoid using stimulants because you may become very tired when they wear off.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Ride more slowly than you would normally.
Start slowing earlier than you would normally.
Increase your following distance.
Not communicate with the passenger while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not communicate with the passenger while riding.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle, so it handles differently. Ride slower than usual, slow down sooner, and stay farther back from other vehicles. Always warn your passenger about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: Who should set the pace in a group of riders?

options.text: The leader
The riders just behind the leader
The rider in back
The oldest rider

questions.correctAnswerText: The rider in back
questions.explanation: The last rider in the group should set the pace. This makes sure no one gets left behind.

questions.question: What is the minimum following distance you should maintain?

options.text: One second
Two seconds
Three seconds
Four seconds

questions.correctAnswerText: Two seconds
questions.explanation: Keep a minimum of two seconds between your motorcycle and the vehicle ahead. In bad weather or poor conditions, increase this to at least three seconds.

questions.question: What does an integrated braking system do?

options.text: Applies partial rear braking when the front brake is applied.
Applies partial front braking when the rear brake is applied.
Applies equal braking to both front and rear brakes when either is applied.
Remembers the braking force the rider usually uses.

questions.correctAnswerText: Applies partial front braking when the rear brake is applied.
questions.explanation: An integrated braking system is a type of linked braking system. When you use the rear brake, it also applies some front braking. Check your motorcycle's owner's manual to learn more about your braking system.

questions.question: Before a passenger rides with you, you should tell them to do everything below except:

options.text: Get on the motorcycle after you start the engine.
Sit as far forward as possible.
Stay a large distance away from you.
Keep their legs away from the muffler and chains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay a large distance away from you.
questions.explanation: Tell your passenger to mount after you start the engine. They should sit as close to you as possible without crowding you, and hold onto the handholds or your waist. They should keep their legs away from the muffler, chains, and other moving parts.

questions.question: What should you know about the oily strip in the center of a traffic lane?

options.text: It is never safe for motorcycles.
It is usually safe unless the road is wet.
You should always avoid it because other parts of the lane are better.
It improves traction for motorcycle tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is usually safe unless the road is wet.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in a strip down the center of traffic lanes. When the road is dry, this strip still provides enough grip for motorcycles. The strip is usually only two feet wide, so you can often ride to one side of it while staying in the center lane.

questions.question: How should a group of motorcycles ride through a curve?

options.text: In a staggered formation.
In a single-file formation.
In a side-by-side formation.
Using both lanes if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: In a single-file formation.
questions.explanation: Although staggered formation is normal, groups should switch to single-file when taking curves, making turns, entering highways, or leaving highways.

questions.question: Why should you not move to the far side of your lane when being passed?

options.text: The passing vehicle may return to your lane too soon.
You might block another vehicle from passing.
The side nearest the passing vehicle is safer.
You will feel more wind blast from the passing vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The passing vehicle may return to your lane too soon.
questions.explanation: Do not ride on the far side of your lane when being passed. This might encourage the passing driver to return to your lane before it is safe to do so.

questions.question: What should you do to stay safe at night when motorcycles are hard to see?

options.text: Slow down.
Use your horn repeatedly.
Avoid riding at night.
Stay directly in front of other vehicles to use their headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: To ride safely at night, slow down, increase your following distance, use the headlights of the car ahead to see farther, use your high beam unless following or meeting another vehicle, and be flexible with your lane position.

questions.question: What does a linked braking system do?

options.text: Connects front and rear brakes so both brake when either lever is used.
Connects the front brake to the gear shifter to apply braking when downshifting.
Connects the rear brake to a foot control.
Connects the rear brake to a handlebar switch.

questions.correctAnswerText: Connects front and rear brakes so both brake when either lever is used.
questions.explanation: A linked braking system connects the front and rear brakes together. When you use either brake lever, it applies braking to both brakes. Check your owner's manual for details about your motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: When is it most important to flash your brake light?

options.text: When passing another vehicle.
When you need to slow down quickly.
When there is a stop sign ahead.
When your turn signals do not work.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you need to slow down quickly.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's single brake light is not as obvious as the two larger brake lights on cars and trucks. Flash your brake light to alert others, especially when you slow down faster than expected.

questions.question: Which is a poor reason to sound your horn?

options.text: A driver next to you is following the car ahead too closely.
A parked car has someone in the driver's seat.
You want people to notice your motorcycle.
You are passing a pedestrian in the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: You want people to notice your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Sound your horn to alert vehicles or pedestrians that may move into your path. If a driver is following too closely, someone is in a parked car, or a pedestrian is in the street, use your horn as a safety warning as you pass.

questions.question: When choosing where to position yourself in a lane, you should:

options.text: Always ride in the center of the lane.
Always ride on the left side of the lane.
Always ride on the right side of the lane.
Change your position based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your position based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position. Ride where other drivers can see you best and where you have space around you on all sides.

questions.question: To control a motorcycle best, a rider should:

options.text: Sit with arms fully extended.
Use arms to hold the body up.
Keep knees away from the gas tank.
Keep feet firmly on the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep feet firmly on the footrests.
questions.explanation: Sit so your arms control the motorcycle, not hold you up. Bend your arms slightly at the handgrips. Keep your knees against the gas tank and feet firmly on the footrests to stay balanced.

questions.question: Motorcycle headlights are:

options.text: Usually stronger than car headlights.
Usually as strong as car headlights.
Usually weaker than car headlights.
Usually larger than car headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually weaker than car headlights.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle headlights are smaller and weaker than car headlights.

questions.question: When riding through a turn, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through the turn.
Keep your arms straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head and eyes to look through the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes to look through the turn.
questions.explanation: Look through the turn to where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks while braking on dry pavement, you should:

options.text: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake, then apply it again quickly.
Release the rear brake and shift down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If your rear brake locks on dry pavement, keep it locked until you stop. You can still control your motorcycle if it stays upright and travels straight.
